title: City-funded tenants and who files as owner of the building
question: Where a City-funded organization rents street-level space, does the owner's tax filing name one of the organization's own officers, or another City payee?
finding: 49 City-funded organizations file as tenant of a commercial space in the vacancy-tax file; an owner filing is on the same parcel for 58. In 0 of them an owner filing carries a surname from the tenant's own list of officers and directors: this test found no grantee renting from an officer. In 3 the owner is itself an organization the City pays (by name), among them Baker Places Inc. at 1156-1164 Valencia St, owner Salvation Army ($53.3 million); Tides Center at 2176-2186 Mission St, owner Sonali Holdings LLC ($4.6 million); San Francisco Bay Area Theatre Company at 2761-2791 24th St, owner Brava for the Women In the Arts ($4.0 million).
how: In the Commercial Vacancy Tax file an owner and each tenant of the same parcel file separately, each tied by its location number to a business registration. Tenants are matched by registered name to profiled City-funded nonprofits and to payees paid $250,000 or more since fiscal 2019; banks and retail chains are left out. For profiled nonprofits every surname of an officer, director or key employee on the tax returns on disk is looked for among the words of the owner filings on that parcel. Owner names are also matched by name to City payees.
limits: The file covers street-level commercial space in the named neighborhood commercial districts only, a small part of where grantees rent; offices on upper floors and anything outside those districts are not in it. An owner that is a company hides its members: only the Secretary of State's statement of information would show whether an officer stands behind it. Owners that read as people or private trusts are not named. The owner-to-payee match is by name.
